---
title: "ENS de Lyon: NGS practicals"
subtitle: "Spatial transcriptomics (Visium) and integration with scRNA-seq"
---

**Audience:** M2 students, ENS de Lyon. **Data:** Visium ([GSE241124](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE241124)) and scRNA-seq ([GSE241132](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE241132)) of the same donor, at four timepoints (healthy skin, day 1, day 7, day 30 after wounding).

::: {.callout-important}
## The notebook
[**Open the practical notebook (web version)**](notebooks/Analysis_open.ipynb), or download it to work on it: [`Analysis_open.ipynb`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sarnatas/skinwound/main/ens-ngs/notebooks/Analysis_open.ipynb) (right-click, *save link as*). It is a single file, with no helper module to install.

The web version shows the instructions and the hints, but **no results**: the figures appear when *you* run your own analysis.

Course slides: [`NGS_practicals_2026.pdf`](slides/NGS_practicals_2026.pdf).
:::

## What you will do

1. Quality control and filtering of Visium spots and genes, normalisation, dimensionality reduction and clustering.
2. Think about **batch effects**, and when *not* to correct them.
3. Analyse the matching scRNA-seq data of the same donor and **annotate cell types** from marker genes.
4. **Annotate the spatial clusters** and **deconvolve** the spots with Cell2location.
5. Read the results: *where* are the cell types, *when*, and *next to whom*?

## How we work

The notebook is a **guide**, not an exercise sheet. It lists the steps of the analysis and the questions to discuss; **you write most of the code** and you are expected to explore the tools (`scanpy`, `squidpy`, `spatialdata`, `spatialdata_plot`): read their documentation, try things, look at what the objects contain. We start with **one sample at a time**, and put them together later.

- Each part has a **Goal** and **questions to discuss** together, then empty cells for your code.
- **Hints** are folded. Open one only after you have tried. Full solutions are given only for the parts where it is easy to get stuck for technical reasons (file formats, data structures, known software traps), never for the analysis choices (filtering, normalisation, clustering...): those are yours.
- A few **custom functions** are already written in the notebook, each with an explanation of why it exists.
- Write your **choices and reasons** in the notes cells: they matter more than the code.
- At the end of the course you **deliver your own notebook**, answering a question you chose.

## Setup

**1. Start a virtual machine (VM) on Biosphere.** Preliminary steps:

1. Connect to the [Biosphere catalogue](https://biosphere.france-bioinformatique.fr/catalogue/) (RAINBio tab).
2. Search for the [Jupyter appliance](https://biosphere.france-bioinformatique.fr/catalogue/appliance/131/).
3. Once on the page, press the green button **RUN** (top right), then **Advanced Configuration and Start**.
4. Name your VM, and select **UEENS-LYON NGS26** in *Group to use*.
5. In *Cloud*, select **meso-psmn-cirrus**.
6. In *Cloud Flavor*, select an appropriate configuration for the VM: **standard.8c32g**, meaning 8 CPU cores and 32 GB RAM.
7. Press **Start Now**.
8. Switch to the **MyVM** tab. Once the VM is ready (approximately 15 minutes after creating it), you should see **https** and **Params** on the left. Press **Params** and copy your `JUPYTER_TOKEN`. Then press **https** and continue to the login screen, where you paste the token.

**2. Python environment.** In the VM, download [`environment.yml`](../environment.yml) and install the environment:

```bash
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate skinwound
pip install ipykernel
conda run -n skinwound python -m ipykernel install --user --name skinwound --display-name "Python skinwound"
```

Once you open the notebook, remember to select the corresponding kernel: click on the top right where "Python 3 (ipykernel)" is written, and select **Python skinwound**.

**3. Data.** The notebook expects one course folder (the variable `BASE` in the paths cell of the notebook, section 0) organised as follows:

```
BASE/
└── data/
    ├── GSE241124_RAW/            Visium: folders Skin/, Wound1/, Wound7/, Wound30/ (Space Ranger outputs)
    ├── GSE241132_RAW/            scRNA-seq: folders PWH27D0/, PWH27D1/, PWH27D7/, PWH27D30/
    │   └── GSE241132_cell_metadata.txt
    ├── paper_marker_genes.csv    marker genes reported in the paper
    └── processed_data/           the Cell2location output computed by the instructors
```

The raw data are public on GEO and are **not** stored in this repository. On the course machines the folder is already prepared: ask the instructors for its location. Your own checkpoints are written to `BASE/my_results/`.
